cpuProfileInterpretation.finding: Repeated UTC date creation/conversion in per-collaborator classification across the full period is a measured optimization candidate. This profile does not establish the origin of all snapshot bytes or all route latency.

limitations: One dedicated staging administrator, one project and one group. No viewer or division coverage established by this run.
Internal Docker bridge HTTP only: excludes TLS, Nginx, browser rendering, LCP and client network.
Sequential phases with differing CPU steal. Observed latency reductions are not an isolated causal estimate of cache benefit.
Jobs disabled only in the temporary HTTP process. Existing staging API and its jobs remained running; production worker topology/pool/resource limits were not fully reproduced.
Temporary HTTP process added a pool of up to eight connections to the shared staging database.
Three warmup passes per route; 100 measured requests per route planned, concurrency two, dispatch capped at two requests per second. Monthly phase stopped early.
Each first-navigation result has n=1; no cold p95 or cold acceptance can be inferred.
Pool fractions cover only intervals sampled during the measured warm workload; no cold/refresh or 24-hour acceptance.
Query wall instrumentation includes pool wait, database/network delay and callback scheduling; it is not database CPU time. Shared-work attribution can follow the owning request.

CPU profile is a separate single point-summary request after 16 seconds to expire response cache; excluded from cohort latencies. Sample fractions are statistical self samples, not exact CPU milliseconds.
Monthly phase incomplete after five consecutive host steal samples at or above 50%; partial cohort p95 suppressed.
No write/cross-session invalidation test in this run. Normal API authentication/session bookkeeping and application-managed derived refreshes can write operational state.
No production changes, persistent staging environment/deployment changes, business edits, migrations, backup changes or retention application.

nextSteps.action: Optimize date/calendar preparation locally once per monthly computation while preserving exact per-collaborator arrays, holidays, absences and financial output; validate with parity and large-period cases.
Investigate host CPU steal; the below-5% infrastructure target remains unmet. Repeat comparable cohorts with stable host capacity.
Validate response-only candidate with viewer/access scopes, external writes and browser navigation before considering activation in production. Monthly remains unapproved for latency.
Complete cold, warm and after-write coverage, frontend/LCP and production 24-hour/seven-day observation without changing backups.
